title: Citric Acid Liquid (RO Membrane Cleaning Grade)
description: Organic acid cleaner for RO membrane descaling and fouling removal.

details.longDescription:
Citric acid liquid for RO membranes (C6H8O7, CAS 77-92-9) is a ready-to-use low-pH membrane cleaner: a 2–3% buffered citric acid solution at pH 3–4, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC from stock in Muscat in 25 kg and 200 kg drums and 1,000 L IBCs; for beverage, dairy and pharmaceutical water systems, ask whether a food-grade lot is available. Citric acid is the mild, biodegradable acid chosen for membranes because it chelates iron, manganese and calcium as it dissolves scale, and it does not attack polyamide, seals or stainless steel the way hydrochloric acid can.

What it removes. Calcium and magnesium carbonate scale, and the iron, manganese and aluminium hydroxide deposits that colour a fouled membrane brown or grey. It does not dissolve calcium, barium or strontium sulphate scale, which needs an alkaline chelant or specialised cleaner, and it does not remove biofilm, organics or silica; those need the alkaline cleaner, and membrane makers recommend the alkaline clean first as the general rule, a permeate flush, then the acid clean; the acid clean goes first only when the foulant is known to be mainly carbonate scale or iron, because acid can set organic and biological foulants. The RO membrane chemicals guide linked on this page covers diagnosis.

How to use it. Fill the CIP tank, warm the solution to 35–40 °C (never above the membrane maker's limit), circulate at low flow for a few minutes to displace feed water, then recirculate for one to four hours, soaking for the second half if the fouling is heavy. Watch the pH: if it rises by more than about half a unit the acid is being consumed by scale, so dose more or replace the solution. Flush with permeate until the pH returns to normal before restarting, and record flux and differential pressure before and after. Clean when normalised flux falls 10% or differential pressure rises 15%, not later; scale that has hardened needs more cycles.

Handling: the solution is acidic and non-flammable; citric acid is classified as causing serious eye irritation (H319), and the classification of the supplied solution is given on its safety data sheet, so wear gloves and goggles, keep it off concrete and mild steel, and store drums closed and shaded. Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis, a technical data sheet with the cleaning procedure and a GHS safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC. Request a quote with the pack size and the membrane area you clean, and our team will size the CIP volume.
applications: RO cleaning in food and beverage plants (ask for a food-grade lot)
technicalSpecs: Hazard: citric acid causes serious eye irritation (H319); see the SDS for the supplied solution

title: Sodium Hydroxide Based Alkaleen Cleaner
description: Alkaline cleaner for organic fouling and biological growth removal from RO membranes.

details.longDescription:
Alkaleen is a formulated alkaline cleaner for reverse osmosis membranes from Global Chemicals LLC, based on sodium hydroxide (NaOH, CAS 1310-73-2) with surfactants and dispersants. Diluted for use, the cleaning solution contains about 0.1% sodium hydroxide, which gives a pH of around 12; a cleaning cycle takes one to two hours, at no more than 30–35 °C depending on the membrane maker's limits. It is packed in 25 kg packs, 200 kg drums and IBCs, from stock in Muscat.

How it works: at high pH, fats and oils saponify, proteins and humic matter dissolve, and the surfactants and dispersants loosen and lift biofilm and organic deposits that an acid cleaner leaves behind. The high pH also helps remove silica and colloidal fouling. Standard membrane practice is to clean with the alkaline solution first, to clear organic and biological fouling, and then with an acid cleaner for scale and metal oxides, because acid applied first can fix organic fouling more firmly to the membrane.

Using it: it is for polyamide thin-film composite membranes in desalination, brackish-water, industrial and wastewater RO systems; it is not for cellulose acetate membranes, which tolerate only a narrow pH range. Membrane manufacturers set pH and temperature limits together — the higher the pH, the lower the maximum temperature — so check the element maker's cleaning limits before use. Make up the solution in RO permeate free of chlorine, circulate at low pressure and the recommended flow, soak and recirculate, and check pH during the clean, adding cleaner if it falls. Flush with permeate until the outlet pH is back to feed level before the acid step or return to service.

Handling and storage: the concentrate is alkaline and corrosive. It causes severe skin burns and eye damage (H314), and products of this type ship as UN 1719, caustic alkali liquid, n.o.s., or UN 1824, sodium hydroxide solution, Class 8 — follow SDS section 14 for this product. Never mix it with acid cleaners or acids; the reaction is violent and gives off heat. It attacks aluminium, zinc and tin. Keep containers closed in a cool, shaded store, wear a face shield, alkali-resistant gloves and apron, and keep an eyewash nearby. Neutralise spent solution before discharge as local rules require. Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis and a GHS safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, 2–3 days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the membrane type, system size, quantity and delivery site.

faqs.question: What is RO antiscalant and why is it critical for reverse osmosis plants in Oman?
faqs.answer: RO antiscalant is a chemical dosed continuously into the feed water of reverse osmosis systems to prevent mineral scale deposition on membrane surfaces. As RO membranes reject dissolved salts and concentrate them in the reject stream, the concentration of scale-forming minerals (calcium, carbonate, sulphate, silica, barium) rises sharply. Without antiscalant, these minerals crystallise on the membrane surface, permanently reducing water flux and salt rejection. Oman has one of the world's highest per-capita desalination capacities, with major SWRO plants at Ghubrah, Barka, Sohar, Al Qurayyat, and Salalah. In Oman's high-TDS seawater and brackish water sources, RO antiscalant is essential to sustaining membrane performance and plant uptime.

faqs.question: What is the correct dosing rate for RO antiscalant in Oman's seawater desalination plants?
faqs.answer: In seawater RO (SWRO) plants in Oman — operating at recovery rates of 35–45% — RO antiscalant is typically dosed at 2–5 mg/L in the RO feed water. The precise dose depends on the seawater chemistry (TDS, calcium, magnesium, sulphate, silica concentrations in the feed), the system recovery rate, and the concentration factor in the reject stream. At higher recovery rates (above 45%), higher antiscalant doses are needed. For brackish water RO systems operating at 70–85% recovery in Oman's interior, dosing rates of 3–8 mg/L are typical. Ask us for a dosage projection from the antiscalant manufacturer’s software, matched to the specific feed water analysis of each plant.

faqs.question: Which scale compounds does RO antiscalant prevent in high-TDS feed water?
faqs.answer: RO antiscalant is formulated to inhibit the most common scale types encountered in Oman's seawater and brackish water desalination. These include calcium carbonate (CaCO₃, the most prevalent scale in RO systems), calcium sulphate (CaSO₄·2H₂O, gypsum, common in high-sulphate seawater), barium sulphate (BaSO₄, extremely insoluble, common in oilfield-associated produced water), strontium sulphate (SrSO₄), silica (SiO₂, amorphous, a challenging scale requiring specialist formulations), and iron hydroxide (from pre-treatment system carry-over). Multi-component antiscalant formulations containing phosphonates, polycarboxylates, and co-polymers are designed to address all these scale types simultaneously, which is critical for complex Omani seawater chemistry.

faqs.question: How does RO antiscalant extend membrane life in Oman's desalination plants?
faqs.answer: RO membranes (thin-film composite polyamide) have a design life of 5–7 years under optimal conditions. Scale deposition accelerates membrane degradation by abrading and blinding the membrane surface, increasing feed-side pressure drop, and forcing more frequent, harsher chemical cleaning. Antiscalant extends membrane life by preventing scale nucleation — keeping dissolved minerals in solution rather than allowing them to crystallise on the membrane surface. Well-dosed antiscalant programmes extend cleaning intervals from monthly to quarterly, reducing the chemical and mechanical stress of each clean-in-place (CIP) cycle. In Oman's large desalination plants, extending membrane replacement cycles by even six months represents significant capital cost savings given the number of elements installed.

faqs.question: What happens if RO antiscalant is under-dosed or stops being dosed?
faqs.answer: Under-dosing or cessation of RO antiscalant dosing causes rapid scale formation on membranes, typically within hours to days depending on the water chemistry and recovery rate. Early indicators include rising feed-to-reject differential pressure, declining normalised permeate flow, and increasing salt passage. Severe scaling can cause permanent flux loss and surface damage that cannot be restored by chemical cleaning. In Oman's SWRO plants treating high-sulphate seawater, calcium sulphate scale is particularly dangerous because it is poorly soluble even in acid cleaning solutions. Antiscalant dosing pump failure alarms and low-level tank alarms are therefore critical safety controls in Oman's desalination plant SCADA systems. Global Chemicals LLC recommends maintaining minimum 30 days' antiscalant stock on-site at all times.
